$comment: The fleet manifest (docs/MECHANIZATION_PLAYBOOK.md, Conversion 3) — the single source of the metro fleet, served at https://districtry.com/metros.json by the Pages deploy. Runtime behavior is deliberately unchanged: the app never fetches this file. It is consumed at GENERATION time — `generate_metro_files.py --sync-fleet` projects these entries (minus `repo`) into each fork's worksheet metro_explorers, and the weekly fleet-status workflow reads `repo` to aggregate across forks. Launching metro N+1 means: add its entry here, then run --sync-fleet + regenerate in each fork (a regeneration PR, never a hand edit). The `tag`, `landing_name`, `blurb` and `scope` fields drive the ROOT LANDING PAGE (scripts/build_landing_page.py) and coverage map (scripts/build_coverage_map.py) and are deliberately fleet-level: sync_fleet projects a whitelist into each worksheet's metro_explorers, so these four never reach an app. `tag` is the instance tag the brand spec sets in the wordmark (districtry / il); `landing_name` is the AREA a reader picks. `label` is what the apps' own switcher and handoff call the place: Illinois carries `label: "Illinois"` (renamed from Chicago on 2026-08-25) because the instance serves 89 counties and a reader sent there is not being sent to a city — `id` stays `chicago`, since it keys the instance's own THIS_METRO. `url` is what the landing page links, and since R5 they ARE districtry.com paths — which is also what the apps' own sibling-metro switcher shows, so a change here reaches both surfaces by `--sync-fleet` + regenerate and never by editing an app. `bbox` is the PORTAL HAND-OFF box, not the instance's own `metro_bbox`: it answers 'if a point falls outside the instance you are in, which sibling should be offered', and validate_index refuses a bbox containing ANOTHER metro's center. Michigan is where the two had to part company. Its TIGERweb county fabric is water-inclusive, so the state's own bbox runs west across Lake Michigan to -90.42 and swallows both Chicago's center (41.8781, -87.6298) and Wisconsin's (44.9, -89.565) — il and wi both failed the gate on it. The shipped box is Michigan's county fabric clipped to lng >= -87.60 (measured, not chosen): six western-UP counties — Baraga, Dickinson, Gogebic, Houghton, Iron, Ontonagon — therefore sit outside the HAND-OFF box and are offered Wisconsin instead, which is exactly what they did before Michigan existed, since wi's own bbox already covers them. Michigan's app still ANSWERS there (its `metro_bbox` is untouched and full-state); only the portal's tie-break is wrong, and no rectangle can fix it because the western UP shares Wisconsin's longitudes. Front-door routing no longer uses a rectangle tie-break at all: a CONTESTED point is settled against each instance's own published coverage ring (scripts/build_landing_page.py's resolveMetro), which fixed Marquette, Escanaba, Sister Bay, Dubuque and Rock Island. The four western-UP counties left over sit outside this clipped box, so the ring is never consulted for them; restoring the full box is an open question in mi/WATCH.md. `scope` is a short (2-4 word) ground-truth phrase for how much of the place is covered — 'X counties' for a partial state, 'all N counties' for a complete one, 'N boroughs'/'1 city' for a city instance — read by the landing page's place rows and the coverage-map legend; it says the same thing `blurb`'s prose already says in more words, so keep the two in agreement when either changes.

metros.label: Illinois
metros.blurb: 93 counties. Wards, county boards, police districts and beats, school zones, judicial subcircuits, and the people who hold those seats.

metros.label: New York City
metros.blurb: Boroughs, City Council and community districts, NYPD precincts and sectors, school zones, and the state and federal seats above them.

metros.label: San Francisco
metros.blurb: Supervisor districts, neighborhoods, police districts, school attendance areas, and the state and federal seats above them.

metros.label: Wisconsin
metros.blurb: County boards, circuit courts, wards and aldermanic districts across all 72 counties — clerk to Court of Appeals — plus school districts, cities, villages and towns, and the Assembly, Senate and U.S. House seats, and who holds those.

metros.label: Iowa
metros.blurb: All 99 counties: supervisor districts with each county's own election plan, townships and cities, school districts, ZIP codes and post offices — and the Iowa Senate, House and U.S. House seats, and who holds those.

metros.label: Michigan
metros.blurb: All 83 counties: commissioner districts, compiled by the state from the plan each county's apportionment commission files — plus townships and charter townships, cities and villages, school districts, and the Michigan Senate, House and U.S. House seats, and who holds those.
